name: New York

regulator.name: New York Department of State, Division of Licensing Services

law.name: Uniform Athlete Agents Act (General Business Law art. 39-E, sections 899 to 899-p)

covers_nil_agents: Yes. New York's 2022 NIL law (S.5891-F/A.5115-E) says agents who represent college athletes on NIL deals must be registered under GBL art. 39-E.
summary: Register with the Department of State. $100, good for 2 years. Athletes can cancel within 5 days.

steps.text: Fill out the Athlete Agent Application (DOS-1640)

steps.detail: This is what the Department of State charges. Pay by check, money order or card form. No cash.

steps.text: Mail it to the Division of Licensing Services
Register with each school's compliance office, if it asks
steps.detail: Most schools have their own agent sign-up.

steps.text: Use a written contract with all required items
steps.detail: Your pay and how it's figured, anyone else being paid, expenses, services, length and date signed.

steps.text: Put the warning to the student-athlete in bold capital letters near their signature
steps.detail: Use the exact words the law gives. New York's warning says the athlete can cancel within 5 days, not 14.

steps.text: Tell the athlete before they sign that signing may cost them eligibility
Give the athlete a copy when they sign
Tell the athletic director in writing within 72 hours of signing
steps.detail: Or before the athlete's next game, whichever comes first. The athlete may cancel within 5 days.

steps.text: Remind the athlete to show each NIL deal to their school before signing it
steps.detail: This is the athlete's job under New York's NIL law. The school tells them if anything in it clashes with school rules.

steps.text: Date the contract the day it's signed
steps.detail: State law and federal law (SPARTA) both ban pre-dating or post-dating it.
Names and addresses of your athletes, every contract and what you spent to recruit each one. The Secretary of State can inspect them.

steps.text: Never give anything of value to an athlete or anyone else before they sign, or make false promises
steps.detail: New York has no 72-hour exception for gifts. Breaking this is a class A misdemeanor, or a felony if your registration is suspended or revoked.
Your registration lasts 2 years. The Department of State lists the renewal fee as $50.

watch_list.item: Federal Protect College Sports Act of 2026 (S.4668)
watch_list.status: Passed the Senate on Sept 28, 2026. The House is out until Nov 9 and leaders say it won't pass as-is. It dies if not enacted by Jan 3, 2027.
watch_list.impact: It would require every NIL agent to register in a state, cap agent fees at 5% of an endorsement deal and limit contracts to the athlete's eligibility.

review_notes: Fee conflict: GBL 899-g says $300 to register and $150 to renew, but the Department of State's page says $100 and $50. The app uses the Department's numbers. Ask the Division of Licensing Services (518-474-4429) which is right.
The NIL law was added as Education Law 6438-a by S.5891-F/A.5115-E (2022), but the Senate's site now shows a different 6438-a. Confirm the current section number of the NIL law on nysenate.gov.
contract_warning: Warning to student-athlete. If you sign this contract: (1) you may lose your eligibility to compete as a student-athlete in your sport; (2) if you have an athletic director, within 72 hours after entering into this contract, both you and your athlete agent must notify your athletic director; and (3) you may cancel this contract within 5 days after signing it. Cancellation of this contract may not reinstate your eligibility.
